title: Depression Over Bay of Bengal Expected to Become Severe Cyclonic Storm by Nov. 17
dek: India’s weather department says a depression in the southeast Bay of Bengal will strengthen into a severe cyclonic storm by Nov. 17, bringing rain to Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh coasts later this week.
author: Meridian Newsroom

image.alt: Satellite view of Tropical Cyclone Fani churning through the Bay of Bengal in April 2019 (file photo, not the current system)

keyPoints: The India Meteorological Department (IMD) said a depression formed on Sunday over the southeast and adjoining southwest Bay of Bengal, about 700 km west-southwest of Port Blair, ANI reported.
IMD forecast that the system would become a cyclonic storm over the central south and west-central Bay of Bengal on Nov. 16 and a severe cyclonic storm on Nov. 17, ANI reported.
The Hindu, citing IMD, said the system is expected to bring rain to north coastal districts of Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal, and to move toward the Andhra Pradesh coast around Nov. 19.
PTI, via HinduBusinessLine, reported IMD saying heavy rain is likely in some West Bengal districts from Nov. 19 to 21.
Forecast tracks and intensity can change; Meridian has not independently verified the track beyond the IMD statements quoted by these outlets.
body:
The India Meteorological Department (IMD) said on Sunday that a depression had formed over the southeast and adjoining southwest Bay of Bengal, and that it is likely to strengthen into a severe cyclonic storm by Nov. 17. The system was centred near latitude 9.0 degrees north and longitude 86.9 degrees east at 5:30 a.m. IST on Sunday, about 700 km west-southwest of Sri Vijaya Puram (Port Blair) in the Andaman Islands, according to the IMD statement reported by ANI.

## What the forecast says

ANI reported that the IMD expects the system to become a cyclonic storm over the central parts of the south and adjoining west-central Bay of Bengal on Nov. 16, and to intensify into a severe cyclonic storm over the west-central Bay on Nov. 17. The depression had moved north-northwestwards from a well-marked low-pressure area over the southeast Bay, ANI reported.

The Hindu, in its Sunday top-news report, said the depression is expected to strengthen into a severe cyclonic storm by Nov. 17 and that the system, which The Hindu calls Cyclone Akvan, is expected to move toward the Andhra Pradesh coast around Nov. 19. Its rain forecast covers north coastal Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and the Karaikal area.

HinduBusinessLine, citing PTI, reported that the system is very likely to move north-northwestward and that IMD expects it to bring heavy rain to some West Bengal districts from Nov. 19 to 21.

## Terms used by the weather service

IMD classifies a depression as an intense low-pressure system whose maximum sustained surface wind speed ranges between 17 and 33 knots (31 to 61 km/h), ANI reported. A cyclonic storm and a severe cyclonic storm are higher categories on the same scale. The forecast stages are IMD’s own; Meridian has not verified how the system will develop.

## Recent systems

ANI’s report describes this as a new system following recent cyclones over the Bay of Bengal. IMD warned of further intensification, ANI reported.

Residents on the Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, Andhra Pradesh and West Bengal coasts should follow official IMD bulletins for updated tracks, wind speeds and rainfall warnings. Meridian will update this story if IMD revises its forecast.
